props.gloss_en: the mishna: on the second three fasts they are forbidden in work, bathing, smearing, wearing shoes and marital relations
the mishna: and they lock the bathhouses
the mishna: these [last seven] exceed the first ones in that on them they sound the alarm and lock the shops
R' Yirmeya bar Abba: the verse says 'sanctify a fast, call an assembly' -- like an assembly-day: as work is forbidden on it, so on a fast
R' Yirmeya bar Abba (as R' Zeira had it from him): 'gather the elders' -- like the gathering of elders, which is by day, the fast too is by day
Rav Huna: the gathering is from the morning

Abaye: from morning to midday we look into the town's affairs; then a quarter of the day we read in the Torah and the haftara; then we ask for mercy -- as it says 'they read in the book of the Torah a quarter of the day, and a quarter they confessed and prostrated' (Neh 9:3)

the stam: it is written 'there gathered to me all who trembled at the words of the God of Israel over the trespass of the exiles' (Ezra 9:4), and 'at the evening offering I rose from my fast and spread my hands to the Lord' (Ezra 9:5) -- the gathering first, the prayer after
Rav Chisda: whatever is on account of mourning, e.g. the Ninth of Av and a mourner, is forbidden in hot water and in cold
Rav Chisda: whatever is on account of pleasure, e.g. a public fast -- in hot water forbidden, in cold permitted
the baraita: all who are obligated in immersion immerse in their usual way, on the Ninth of Av and on Yom Kippur
Rav Chana bar Ketina: [the baraita] was needed only for the hot springs of Tiberias
R' Chanina segan hakohanim: the house of our God is worth losing an immersion over once a year
Rav Pappa: [R' Chanina speaks] of a place where cold water is not common
the baraita: when they said work is forbidden, they said it only by day; at night it is permitted
the baraita: when they said shoes are forbidden, they said it only in town; on the road permitted -- going out he puts them on, entering town he removes them
the baraita: when they said bathing is forbidden, they said it only of the whole body; face, hands and feet are permitted -- and so you find with one under a ban and a mourner
a mourner is forbidden to put his finger into hot water (cited as Rav Sheshet's at 13a.9, as Rav Chisda's at 13b.2 and 13b.6)
the stam: the baraita is about hot water; its 'and so you find with one under a ban and a mourner' refers to the remaining [clauses], not to bathing
R' Yosei hakohen: it happened that R' Yosei b. R' Chanina's sons died, and he bathed in cold water all seven days
the stam: there his mournings came one upon another
the baraita: if his mournings came one after another and his hair grew heavy, he may lighten it with a razor and launder his garment in water
Rav Chisda: with a razor, not with scissors; in water, not with natron nor with sand (at 13b.4 he adds: nor with ahala)
Rava: a mourner may bathe in cold water all seven days
Rava: just as with meat and wine [which a mourner may have]
the baraita: a grown woman may not make herself unattractive in the days of mourning for her father (inferred by the stam: a young girl may)
the stam: no -- [the baraita speaks of] painting the eyes and arranging the hair
Rava (second version): a mourner is forbidden [to bathe] in cold water all seven days
the stam: there [meat and wine] he takes to ease his dread
Rav Chisda: this is to say, a mourner is forbidden to launder all seven days
the law: a mourner is forbidden to bathe his whole body, in hot water or in cold, all seven days
the law: his face, hands and feet -- in hot water forbidden, in cold permitted
the law: smearing [with oil], even the least amount, is forbidden
the law: and if it is to remove dirt, it is permitted
Rav Yehuda (expounded by Rav Yitzchak): an individual who accepted a fast upon himself prays the prayer of a fast
and where does he say it? between 'who redeems' and 'who heals'
in [the blessing] 'who hears prayer'
Rav Yitzchak: may an individual fix a blessing for himself? [he may not]
the baraita: the only difference between an individual and a community is that this one prays eighteen and that one nineteen
the stam: no -- 'community' is the prayer leader, and [the baraita speaks] of the first three fasts, in which there are not twenty-four
the baraita: the only difference between the first three and the middle three is that on these work is permitted and on those forbidden
the stam, alternatively: on the middle ones too they do not pray twenty-four
the baraita: the only difference between the second three and the last seven is that on these they sound the alarm and lock the shops
Rav Ashi: the mishna is precise too -- in all their other matters [the second three and the last seven] are the same

answered_by.gloss_en: לא, לעולם בחמין; וכן אתה מוצא -- אשארא קאי (= p_stam_vechen_ashara_kai)

answered_by.gloss_en: לא, לעולם שליח צבור, in the first three fasts, which have no twenty-four (= p_stam_rishonot_lo_esrim_vearba; its own attack and defence are obj_ein_bein_rishonot_emtzaiyot)

answered_by.gloss_en: השתא דאתית להכי: עשרים וארבעה נמי לאו שיורא הוא, דקתני לה באידך פירקא -- the twenty-four is taught in the other chapter, so the list does not count it

objections.gloss_en: ותסברא מה אלו דוקא הוא? והא שייר לה תיבה!

answered_by.gloss_en: אי משום תיבה -- לאו שיורא הוא, משום דקא חשיב לה באידך פירקא
